content:
Apple's outgoing CEO Tim Cook made vague remarks during an earnings call that appear to suggest the cost of high Siri AI usage may be higher than we currently expect.

Although it has always been an open secret that unlimited free use of Siri AI is unsustainable and will eventually come at some cost, Cook's comments do seem to point to some bad news…

What we already know

Apple aims to run as much AI computation on-device as possible, which both maximises user privacy and saves Apple from having to pay for AI servers to handle those tasks. However, some tasks still need to run on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute servers, and some require the use of Google Gemini servers.

Using these servers naturally imposes costs on Apple, so it has long seemed clear that Apple would apply the same free-plus-paid model it uses for other chatbots to Siri AI: a limited free tier, with heavy users paying for an additional monthly subscription.

However, the prevailing view so far has been that using Siri AI would only require an iCloud+ subscription, with usage caps potentially tied to the iCloud+ tier — for instance, a 50GB plan coming with a certain usage cap, the 200GB plan getting more, and the 2TB plan getting even more.

This means that many of us would effectively receive higher Siri AI usage allowances automatically as part of our existing iCloud+ plans.

But we may have to pay extra

On the earnings call, a Goldman Sachs analyst asked Cook about this.

His response appeared to go beyond simply saying an iCloud+ subscription is required:

One reading of this is that heavy use of Siri AI is not just a matter of subscribing to iCloud+, but will involve additional add-on charges. In other words, the subscription itself won't automatically bring a higher usage cap — it merely gives users the option to purchase add-ons to raise that cap.

His wording was vague, so this isn't necessarily what he meant. However, if Cook had only wanted to convey that higher usage caps come bundled with an iCloud+ subscription, I would have expected him to say so more clearly. It is precisely because his phrasing was ambiguous that I cannot help suspecting the news may not be good — or, taking a step back, let's assume for argument's sake that Apple hasn't made a final decision yet but is considering the add-on route.

Of course, everything will have to wait until we have a clearer picture of actual Siri AI usage and roughly when we might hit the usage caps. Even if my inference is correct, it may not affect the majority of Apple users. Nevertheless, judging from the experience with existing AI chatbots, many people who find them useful and use them more than just occasionally often end up having to pay for a subscription.

What do you think? Do you agree with my reading of the implications behind Cook's wording? If so, do you think you'd be willing to pay to use Siri AI? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
